publication: Hallager, Godart & Olivier 1989, La rondelle en lineaire A d'Haghia Triada Wc 3024 (HM 1110), BCH 113, 431-437
notes: Rapport-series omission recovered 2005; BCH on Persee open; present in silver

publication: Kopaka 1989, Une nouvelle inscription en lineaire A de Zakros, Kadmos 28, 7-13
notes: Rapport-series omission recovered 2005; present in silver; distinct from the ZA Zb 35/39 rumor item

description: Owens's Corpus of Published Inscriptions in Linear A (COPILA): catalogue of LA inscriptions published, 'rediscovered' or announced after GORILA; classification errors noted (e.g. MO Zg 1 for Zf 1); its 'rediscovered' items = five pseudo-inscriptions on Knossos architectural supports + one incised mark on a Mycenae bronze basin (rejected); its value = the three forgotten documents above
publication: Owens 2005, Corpus of Published Inscriptions in Linear A (COPILA), DO-SO-MO 6, 26-45
notes: BOOKKEEPING row (resource, not an item); pseudo-inscriptions and the Mycenae basin mark explicitly NOT admitted

description: Larnax fragment HM 21.172 with painted inscription, found 1975 by I. Sakellarakis in Tholos E of the Phourni necropolis; announced by Godart at Chaumont, prudently excluded from GORILA IV, re-admitted by Olivier at Salzburg with classification Zc 8; readings: Olivier AB 21f-59-46 (21f dotted) or AB 53-59-46 (53 dotted; sequence attested KH 6.4); Sakellarakis A 306-AB 59-AB 46 (306 dotted); Panagiotopoulos dates sarcophagus + inscription to the final phase of the necropolis, ca. MM II
publication: Panagiotopoulos 2002, Das Tholosgrab E von Phourni bei Archanes (BAR-IS 1014), 59-60, pls. 18, 63-64; Sakellarakis & Sapouna-Sakellaraki 1997, vol. I, 332
notes: Three alternative readings printed; present in silver (check which reading silver carries)

description: PUBLISHED: the 1992 stone offering-table fragment with ten engraved signs; reading ]AB 123 , 57-31-31-60-13 , 10-06-26-77[ (13 dotted); AB 123 (probably the final part of a lost syllabic sequence) attested for the first time in a non-archival inscription; the groups AB 57-31-31-60-13 and AB 10-06-26-77[ are frequent in this genre (libation formula)
publication: Karetsou, Godart & Olivier 2002-2003 [2006], Une nouvelle inscription en lineaire A du sanctuaire de sommet du Mont Iouktas (IO Za 16), Minos 37-38, 437-447
notes: Full reading printed; Minos is open on the journal site (round-1 note, unverified); present in silver

description: INEDIT: clay 'token' ca. 2 cm diameter, <1 cm thick, six signs running along the edge, tops outward, forming an almost complete circle; found in a Second-Palace-period building; support without parallels, hence the Wy prefix; Olivier (autopsy, pers. comm.) reads AB 08-01[ ]02-27-27 (hapax) despite sign-form idiosyncrasies; the long vertical stroke between 08 and 27 = numeral 1 or a divider; circular-layout parallels: HT Wc 3010/3015, SY Za 1, PK Za 15, KN Zc 6/7, KN Zf 31, KN Zf 13 (spiral)
publication: To be published by G. Rethemiotakis (never appeared in Rapports 2006-2021)
notes: ABSENT from silver - genuine gap; Olivier's provisional reading printed in rapport but NO editio princeps through 2021; Younger lists it (round-1 channel)

description: Classification discussion of the 1992 MM IIA fragment: Schoep (forthcoming ABSA suppl.) reads a fragmentary logogram attributable to CH (*164/*165) or LA (AB 180) plus a numeral of four (maybe six) dots preceded by an oblique stroke (tens preceded by the unit sign - an anomaly); Schoep: script undecidable, verso scratches suggest a label, hence Wy 49; Olivier: the fragmentary sign = a ligature (A 548-552) and the dots+stroke = klasmatogram A 743, hence LA; DEL FREO AGREES with Olivier (smooth regular base = tablet or bar, not label; verso scratches accidental cf. KN Gg 995) and keeps KN 49 = the oldest known LA administrative document
publication: Schoep in Macdonald & Knappett, Knossos: Protopalatial Pottery from the Southwest Palace Area (BSA Suppl., forthcoming at rapport date); photo in Huxley (ed.) 2000, Cretan Quests, 62, fig. 34
notes: Present in silver as KN49 (Del Freo/Olivier classification, not Schoep's Wy 49)

description: Jug of MM IIIB - LM IA date with 4 signs incised on the shoulder, still unpublished (per the rapport; the Cretan Quests photo appeared 2000)
publication: Status note; cf. Rapport 1996-2000 sub 2.2.1.3
notes: See Rapport 2006-2010 row for the published reading AB 79-53-30-80; present in silver

description: In course of publication by Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager: small opisthographic tablet fragment from the 1989 Splantzia excavation east of Kastelli, LM I context; announced in the Salzburg and Austin rapports
publication: Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007, New and unpublished Linear A and Linear B inscriptions from Khania, PDIA 5, 7-22; texts also in Hallager 2008, Colloquium Romanum, 359-360
notes: PDIA is open online; present in silver as sided KH97a/KH97b

description: NEW: vase fragment with one sign incised before firing, MM III; the first LA vase inscription from Khania; NUMBERING: Hallager publishes it as KH Zb 1; Del Freo argues LA vase inscriptions are not numbered independently of other inscription types (GORILA V pp. 83-113), hence KH Zb 98
publication: Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007, ibid. (as KH Zb 1)
notes: SILVER FOLLOWS DEL FREO: silver has KHZb98 (not KHZb1) - numbering divergence resolved in silver in Del Freo's favor

description: NEW: roundel with three signs, found out of context in a Geometric-period deposit
publication: Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007, ibid.
notes: Present in silver; LATER: new sign A 373 read on it (Rapport 2006-2010); Del Freo & Zurbach read a tripod-logogram variant instead (Rapport 2016-2021, round-1 row)

description: NEW: fragmentary tablet found (not in situ) 2005 in an LM II layer during arrangement works; NUMBERING: = Hallager's KH 98; Del Freo's 99 presupposes Zb 98 for the vase
publication: Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007, ibid. (as KH 98)
notes: Present in silver as KH99 (Del Freo numbering)

description: NEW: fragmentary tablet found (not in situ) 2005 in an LM IIIA layer (layer later re-dated LM IIIB1, cf. Rapport 2006-2010 on KH 102); NUMBERING: = Hallager's KH 99
publication: Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007, ibid. (as KH 99)
notes: Present in silver as KH100 (Del Freo numbering)

description: Fragmentary coarse-clay handle (00/4831/17), perhaps of an amphora, chance find summer 2000; three incised signs AB 73-01-60 (60 dotted), hapax
publication: Schoep & Driessen 2002-2003 [2006], An Inscribed Handle from Palaikastro (PK Zb 25), Minos 37-38, 77-80
notes: Reading printed; present in silver; LATER: Hopkins 2018 re-reading dispute (AB 73-01-51), rapport 2016-2021 finds it no better (round-1 row)

description: INEDIT: pithos fragment (cat. 7926) with inscription engraved under the rim before firing, found 2003 in room 13 of building 4, LM IB context; announced by Sackett at the AIA 2004 meeting; incomplete sequence ]AB 05-56-08 (hapax); to be published by Schoep (preliminary manuscript seen)
publication: Announced AIA 2004; Schoep publication forthcoming at rapport date
notes: Reading printed in rapport; present in silver

description: NEW: fragmentary tablet found 2000 in an MM III deposit of a cult-vase magazine ~50 m from the palace; broken right and bottom; two ruled lines; sequences AB 28-06-[.]-04 and AB 59-06-80-46, both hapax; CLASSIFICATION DISPUTE: Hallager considers it a votive text intentionally fired and adopts Zg 6 (fn. 33); Del Freo keeps PE 6
publication: Tsipopoulou & Hallager, New Linear A Inscriptions from Petras (announced for SMEA; texts in Hallager 2008, Colloquium Romanum, 359); ed.pr. eventually Hallager 2012 (see Rapport 2011-2015 row)
notes: SILVER FOLLOWS HALLAGER: silver has PEZg6 (not PE6); ERRATUM to round-1: the round-1 checklist diffed PE 6 as a b-class acquisition gap - it is PRESENT under the Zg 6 alias; designation history PE 6 -> PE Zg 6 -> PE <6> (unlocatable) -> PE 6 (relocated 2017, Rapport 2016-2021)

description: NEW: pithos fragment with two inscriptions under the rim: at the left end the sign AB 08 (possibly preceded by another sign) incised AFTER firing; at the right end two signs engraved BEFORE firing: AB 57-54[ (sequence attested KN Za 18); LM IB
publication: Tsipopoulou & Hallager, ibid.; texts in Hallager 2008, 359
notes: Present in silver; READING LATER REVISED after restoration: AB 57-54-39-.[ (Rapport 2011-2015 row)

description: NEW: pithos fragment with an isolated sign AB 08 traced superficially before firing; LM IB
publication: Tsipopoulou & Hallager, ibid.; texts in Hallager 2008, 359
notes: Present in silver; LATER: GORILA Supplement will EXCLUDE it (isolated sign of unsure logographic value, Rapport 2011-2015) - inclusion-criteria divergence flag

description: NEW (numbering fix): flat-based nodule HM 676 with traces of inscription, datable MM II; mentioned by Hallager as Wb 55 (Minoan Roundel II 225, 295 - numbering to be rejected: the Wa 53/54 of Minoan Roundel are anepigraphic) and as Wb 53 (Floreant p. 285); absent from Olivier's rapports; here numbered PH Wb 53
publication: Hallager 1996, Minoan Roundel II, 225, 295; Hallager 1999 in Floreant, 285
notes: DELETED LATER: autopsy (Rapport 2006-2010) shows plant-ligament traces, not writing; inscription suppressed, number 53 kept vacant (Rapport 2011-2015); silver correctly LACKS PHWb53 - absence is the endorsed state

description: INEDIT: gold ring from a neopalatial tomb (Dimopoulou rescue excavation; BCH 124, 994); the second inscription incised on the circular bezel of a ring after KN Zf 13 (Mavrospilio); very small object (6 mm diameter); sequence AB 69-39-59 (hapax) running left to right along the bezel edge; to be published by Dimopoulou & Olivier (Olivier's epigraphic commentary seen by Del Freo)
publication: To be published by Dimopoulou & Olivier (no editio princeps traced in Rapports 2006-2021)
notes: Present in silver as PORZf2 (silver uses POR prefix here but PO in POZc1 - internal sigla inconsistency); reading printed in rapport

description: Two non-joining sherds of a single chalice, LA signs painted dark-on-light [KNSM Sko 187 [+] 188], from Davaras's 1962 excavation of the Skoteino cave ~20 km east of Herakleion; probably LM I; editors' readings: ]vest. , AB 06-69-A301-24[ (69, 301 dotted) for the larger fragment and ]AB 16-67-79[ (all dotted) for the smaller; Del Freo finds the AB 69 identification unconvincing (painted-LA ductus unknown; painted corpus: ARKH Zc 8, KN Zc 6/7, PE Zc 4, PK Zc 13, PO Zg 1)
publication: Perna, Kanta & Tyree [2006], An Unpublished Inscription in Linear A from the Skoteino Cave, Crete (SKO Zc 1), in Studi Fiandra, 321-333
notes: Readings printed (heavily dotted); present in silver

description: INEDITS: five new inscribed 'offering tables' discovered 1987-2000 by Lebessi: Za 8 HM 3825 (two fragments, 1997 + 2000), Za 9 HM 5585 (1987), Za 10 HM 5531 (1995), Za 11 HM 5590 (2000), Za 12 HM 5782 (2000); to be published by Olivier with the rest of the Symi epigraphic material; ALSO: on the already-known but never-studied table Za 4 (HM 5586) the homomorph of B 48 nwa is attested - AB 48 must be added to the LA syllabary table (a Ventris & Chadwick prophecy, Docs p. 40)
publication: To be published by Olivier (appeared: Muhly & Olivier 2008, AE 147 - see Rapport 2006-2010 row)
notes: All five present in silver (SYZa8-SYZa12); AB 48 sign-inventory addition is the headline

description: INEDIT: Tzachili signals two sherds with possible LA inscriptions from the peak sanctuary (Davaras 1973 excavations, MM III) - Del Freo finds those two DOUBTFUL from the photos; on a THIRD sherd the sign ]AB 73[ (dotted) engraved before firing is recognizable = this VRY Zb 2 (?)
publication: Tzachili, Mesominoiki kerameiki apo ton Vrysina. Protes ektimiseis, in 9th Cretological Congress [announcement], 32
notes: Present in silver; READING SUPERSEDED: full publication Tzachili & Georgakopoulos 2015 reads ]AB 34-31[ or ]AB 11-31[ (Rapport 2016-2021, round-1 row: 'earlier Rapport read ]AB 73[')

description: Inscription of three or four signs incised on a vase fragment; 'announced erroneously in the Austin rapport as Zb 35'; still inedit
publication: Unpublished
notes: ABSENT from silver - never published through 2021 (not mentioned in Rapports 2006-2021); genuine pending item since 1996-2000

description: Two ANEPIGRAPHIC roundels bearing on the rim the hieroglyphic seal impressions #135 and #136 (CMS V Suppl. 1B (1993) nos. 326 and 325), not yet classed among the anepigraphic roundels; assigned inscription-numbers under the 'paradoxical but inevitable' practice (fn. 44)
publication: CMS V Suppl. 1B (1993) nos. 325-326; cf. Rapport 1991-1995 pp. 420-421
notes: BOOKKEEPING row - anepigraphic, NOT corpus candidates; matters only for the SA We 3 renumbering

description: Nodulus, ex We 1 (= CHIC #137), renumbered because of {SA Wc 1}/{SA Wc 2}; Olivier initially read (left to right) an arithmogram, a klasmatogram and an isolated syllabogram; after autopsy: the arithmogram is a simple control mark, and the inscription = the sinistroverse sequence of AB 04 and klasmatogram A 708 (K), or alternatively a ligature of the two ('04'+'708'), proposed as new sign A 505bis; A 708 is exclusive to LA
publication: CMS V Suppl. 1B (1993); cf. Rapport 1991-1995 pp. 420-421, 430; Minoan Roundel II 218
notes: ABSENT from silver (only SAMWa1 present for Samothrace) - genuine gap WITH reading in hand; a_ingestible candidate; MM II-III

description: Nodulus found 1999, published by Matsas as We 2 (CMS V Suppl. 3 (2004) no. 343); same findspot and layer as {SA Wc 1}/{SA Wc 2}/We 3, MM II-III; one side bears a seal impression (possibly hieroglyphic, cf. rapport CH section 1.2.2.1); the other an inscription engraved with a stylus; Matsas: ligature A 609 or new ligature AB 08 + A 303 followed by numeral 1 or 10; Olivier (autopsy): ligature AB 08+04 (08 dotted), proposed as new sign A 506bis; the lower-left dot is a stylus perforation from applying a control mark, not a numeral; both signs also exist in CH so the LA attribution is not fully certain, but the exclusive-LA klasmatogram A 708 on twin nodulus We 3 reinforces it
publication: Matsas 2004, CMS V Suppl. 3, no. 343 (as SA We 2)
notes: ABSENT from silver - genuine gap WITH reading in hand; a_ingestible candidate; designation collision Matsas We 2 vs Olivier/Del Freo We 4; round-1 row (from Rapport 2016-2021 fn. 14-15) superseded by this fuller record

description: NEW + published: sealed and inscribed pithos rim found 2000 south of Xeste 2, LM IA context; reading '21' '588' 120 77-08-41-[[.-.-04]] (21, 77, 41 dotted; [[ ]] = erased); no classification proposed in the SMEA article - the designation Zb 13 is assigned by this rapport (Karnava's own scheme would call it Zb 11)
publication: Karnava & Nikolakopoulou 2005, A Pithos Fragment with a Linear A Inscription from Akrotiri, Thera, SMEA 47, 213-225
notes: Present in silver as THEZb13 (Del Freo's number - silver follows the rapport here, but follows the EDITORS for the lamp Zb 15: mixed scheme)

description: NUMBERING NOTE: the rapport fixes the Thera list as Zb 1-4, Zg 5, Zb 6 (House of the Ladies, inedit), THE 7-12 (6 [?] tablet fragments, Delta 18a, 1993, inedits), Zb 13 (Xeste 2 pithos); it REJECTS Karnava's scheme (Michailidou's Room Delta-3 amphora fragment - signs 'ne semblent pas constituer une veritable inscription' - as Zb 6, shifting old 6-9 to 7-10, Xeste 2 = Zb 11); Michailidou's proposed readings for that fragment: A 318-AB 08 / 41 / 27 (all dotted)
publication: Michailidou 2000-2001 [2002], Indications of Literacy in Bronze Age Thera, Minos 35-36, 12-15; Karnava in Horizon (2008), 378
notes: BOOKKEEPING/DIVERGENCE row: silver Thera IDs are a MIXED BAG (THEZb5 AND THEZg5; THEZb6 AND THEZb7; ad-hoc THEfr.1-3/THEtab.4-5; Del Freo's Zb13 + editors' Zb15) - divergence-register candidate

description: INEDITS: six new vase inscriptions found 1997-2005 in ceramic material from the temple of Athena; local clay, engraved before firing, very small fragments of one or two signs: Zb 2 ]AB 56-[ (pithos), Zb 3 ]AB 41-04[ (small closed vase), Zb 4 ]AB 41[, Zb 5 ]AB 08[, Zb 6 ]AB 31[ (31 dotted), Zb 7 AB 27-[ (plus a post-firing sign resembling a ship's prow); all now dated LM IA (Zb 1 re-dated from LM IB/II to LM IA per Zurbach)
publication: To be published by Niemeier & Zurbach in Kadmos (appeared 2015 REORGANIZED as Niemeier, Del Freo & Zurbach, Kadmos 54 - see Rapport 2011-2015 row)
notes: RENUMBERED IN EDITION: 2015 publication keeps Zb 2 (AB 56-29[), Zb 3 (]AB 41-04[), suppresses old Zb 4/5/6 (isolated signs), renumbers Zb 7 -> Zb 4 (]AB 27-86[); silver has MILZb1-4 = the final 2015 state

description: NEGATIVE: Zurbach re-studied the spindle-whorls published by Schliemann 1875, in which Godart had recognized two LA inscriptions; probable dating Troy II or III and comparison with contemporary whorls identify the engraved signs as decorative motifs of a local tradition; same conclusion for vases Schmidt 2444 and 2445
publication: Zurbach 2003, Schriftahnliche Zeichen und Topferzeichen in Troia, Studia Troica 13, 115-116
notes: NEGATIVE VERDICT row - not LA; correctly absent from silver

description: Clay reel-shaped object (h. 3.20 x diam. 2.60-2.65 cm), vertically perforated (necklace element?), five signs incised on the concave surface; found September 1996 inside 'Construction B' of a funerary complex on the Kajrjaka hill near Drama; dating uncertain; Fol & Schmitt: at least three of the five signs are LA, inscription sinistroverse, reading AB 01-51-A 301-[.]-[.] or AB 01-51-A 301-[.]-79 (01, 51, 301, 79 dotted), supported by initial AB 01-51 in KN Zf 31 and HT 95a.1; DEL FREO: published photos do not permit assessment; on the facsimile the first sign = AB 01 is 'plutot discutable'; the local-imitation conclusion is too risky (uncertain date, reading difficulties, support without Bronze-Age Aegean parallel)
publication: Fol & Schmitt 2000, A Linear A Text on a Clay Reel from Drama, South-East Bulgaria?, PZ 75, 56-62
notes: DOUBT FLAG: silver INCLUDES DRAZg1 although Del Freo treats the attribution as unassessable/doubtful; divergence-register candidate

description: Jug handle from Phylakopi (Ashmolean AE 2330), end of phase II / start of phase III (~MM III - LM I), two signs engraved after firing; Driessen: possibly LA, readable A 301-AB 27 or AB 37-27; Del Freo: AB 29 or A 314 not excluded for the second sign; since neither sign is attributable with certainty to the LA repertoire, Sherratt's conclusion is adopted ('one cannot be certain that they actually represent literate signs belonging to this - or any other - system of writing'); the classification MI Zb 3 (Karnava, Younger) is therefore 'discutable' (fn. 62)
publication: Sherratt 2000, Catalogue of Cycladic Antiquities in the Ashmolean Museum, 350-351, pl. 606, fig. 261
notes: DOUBT FLAG: silver INCLUDES MIZb3 although the rapport declines the attribution; divergence-register candidate

description: BOOKKEEPING: the Borda-catalogue no. 9 nodule believed absent from the Pigorini collection is a photographic phantom - plate XLV juxtaposed two photographic plates on which the same nodule HT Wa 1547 appears twice (no. 8 inv. 71976 = pl. XLV:12 and no. 9 = pl. XLV:17); verified in the Museum's photo archive by Del Freo
publication: Del Freo 2002-2003, I noduli del Museo Preistorico-Etnografico 'Luigi Pigorini' provenienti da Haghia Triada, Bullettino di paletnologia italiana 93-95 (N.S. XI-XII), 53-75
notes: Phantom duplicate eliminated; HT Wa 1547 present in silver

description: NEGATIVE: cylindrical alabastron with four signs engraved after firing, three compatible with LA (Egetmeyer: first ~ A 706, second ~ A 339, fourth ~ A 304; third without parallels); origin unknown, stylistically East-Mediterranean/Cypriot, LH IIIA2 - early IIIC; signs could have been added elsewhere/later; a forgery cannot be excluded; DEL FREO: leave this graffito OUT of the LA corpus
publication: Egetmeyer & Zavadil 2004, Ein Spatbronzezeitliches Alabastron aus dem ostlichen Mittelmeerraum mit Graffito, Kadmos 43, 151-158
notes: NEGATIVE VERDICT row - excluded from corpus; correctly absent from silver
